interpretations.question: Is a pole-mount transformer 'facility equipment' under 327 IAC 2-6.1, and where is the facility boundary?
interpretations.position: Pole-mount transformers are treated as facility equipment; the facility boundary is the base of the supporting pole, so any release that reaches the soil beyond the pole base is classified as beyond-boundary.
interpretations.rationale: Pack is empty. Conservative reading chosen to make more releases reportable.

interpretations.question: Is a padmount transformer vault the 'facility' boundary under 327 IAC 2-6.1?
interpretations.position: The padmount transformer vault slab and any secondary containment structure constitute the facility boundary. Releases beyond the vault slab are beyond-boundary. Releases reaching a connected storm drain are treated as reaching a receiving medium regardless of whether the drain is 'at' the facility.
interpretations.rationale: Pack is empty. Conservative reading chosen.

interpretations.question: Is the substation perimeter fence the facility boundary for 327 IAC 2-6.1 purposes?
interpretations.position: The substation perimeter fence marks the facility boundary. Releases on internal impervious containment pads are inside-boundary; releases that penetrate the fence gravel or reach beyond the fence are beyond-boundary.
interpretations.rationale: Pack is empty. Conservative reading chosen.

interpretations.question: Are standby generator belly tanks at service centers 'facility fuel storage' sources?
interpretations.position: Belly tanks at service centers are classified as facility fuel storage. The concrete pad and double-wall secondary containment define the containment boundary; any release that exits secondary containment is classified by actual receiving medium.
interpretations.rationale: Pack is empty. Conservative reading chosen.

interpretations.question: Is fueling at a service center a facility source?
interpretations.position: Service center fueling stations are facility sources with the service center property boundary as the facility boundary.
interpretations.rationale: Pack is empty. Conservative reading chosen.

interpretations.question: Are fleet vehicles in transit treated as transportation sources with no fixed facility boundary?
interpretations.position: Fleet vehicles in transit (on public roads or customer property) are transportation sources with no fixed facility boundary; all releases are classified by actual receiving medium.
interpretations.rationale: Pack is empty. Conservative reading chosen.

interpretations.question: Does a fleet vehicle parked at a work site (not a service center) retain its transportation-source classification?
interpretations.position: Yes. A vehicle at a work site that is not a service center retains its transportation-source classification; the receiving medium governs reportability.
interpretations.rationale: Pack is empty. Conservative reading chosen.

interpretations.question: How is an oil release discovered on customer property classified?
interpretations.position: The source is identified first (which RPL asset?). If an RPL asset, the relevant §7.1 row applies. If a vehicle, the transportation-source classification applies. When the source is uncertain, the release is treated as reportable.
interpretations.rationale: Pack is empty. Conservative reading chosen: uncertain classification defaults to reportable.
